implementation_notes: Go's realization needs no pattern scaffolding: a struct with exported fields and json tags is the DTO, and encoding/json from the standard library marshals and unmarshals it directly, so the classic bean, its accessors and its serializer are all replaced by the language plus stdlib. Keep boundary structs separate from domain and persistence structs even when they look alike: the boundary struct exists to pin wire names, omit or rename fields and absorb validation, while the domain struct stays free to change. encoding/gob or a generated protobuf type is preferred over JSON when the payload is internal and binary.
pitfalls: Only exported fields are marshalled: a lowercase field disappears from the payload without any error.
omitempty conflates the zero value with absence, so legitimate 0/""/nil values vanish and cannot be distinguished on decode - use pointer fields or a presence wrapper when absence matters.

Untyped fields (any) decode numbers as float64 and lose precision and type safety, and decoding is case-insensitive and ignores unknown keys by default, so a strict contract needs DisallowUnknownFields or a validator.
